sample_unit: rural residents with positive screening who underwent endoscopy (implementation phase)
models_evaluated: rural-to-center AI model for H. pylori, atrophic gastritis and intestinal metaplasia from endoscopy images

links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy at rural implementation site versus development-phase accuracy
links.effect: Implementation accuracy: H. pylori 91.3% (development 92.8%), atrophic gastritis 79.9% (88.6%), intestinal metaplasia 63.4% (88.0%). Accuracy was maintained for H. pylori but dropped for premalignant conditions.
links.quote: Implementation-phase diagnostic accuracies were 91.3% (95%CI 88.0%–94.6%), 79.9% (95%CI 72.1%–86.3%), and 63.4% (95%CI 54.7%–71.6%), respectively.

unlisted_practices: Transmitting rural hospital endoscopy images to a tertiary center for AI analysis with results returned promptly
AI preprocessing to exclude low-quality and non-gastric endoscopy images

screen.reason: The study evaluated a prospective implementation of an AI diagnostic model transmitting rural endoscopy images to a tertiary center for analysis during real clinical workflow, but did not test a specific deployment safeguard or practice comparatively.
